cf.title: Add XMLSerialize: version (SQL/XML X076), explicit declaration (SQL/XML X078)

input.subject: XMLSerialize: version and explicit XML declaration

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and the clauses are SQL/XML standard syntax that only core can add. The remaining points are fixable: already-exists-1 asks what the clauses add over xmlroot(), and standards-compat-1, standards-compat-3 and maintenance-fit-2 ask about CONTENT mode output, the warning for '1.1' and per-row checks. Nobody has reviewed the design since message #2, so someone who knows the xml code must settle these.

brief.title: XMLSERIALIZE options for VERSION and explicit XML declaration
brief.problem: XMLSERIALIZE gives no way to add, remove or set the version of the XML declaration in its output. The patch adds SQL/XML features X076 (VERSION) and X078 (explicit XML declaration), which Postgres lists as not supported. The thread does not name users who need them.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds VERSION, INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION and EXCLUDING XMLDECLARATION to XMLSERIALIZE. With neither declaration option, the output keeps a declaration only if the input had one, and VERSION alone adds none. Without INDENT, only the declaration is added, replaced or removed, never with an encoding, and libxml2 checks the version string in both DOCUMENT and CONTENT mode.
user_visible_surface: New XMLSERIALIZE clause: INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION | EXCLUDING XMLDECLARATION.
New keywords in kwlist.h, so a change to the keyword list.
Error for versions libxml2 rejects, such as '2.0', and a warning for versions it does not fully support, such as '1.1'.
sql_features.txt marks X076 and X078 as supported, which shows in information_schema.sql_features.
author_claims: The behavior without the new options is the same as before.
Leaving out the encoding declaration matches what xml_out() does, because the result goes through encoding conversion.
Tom Lane suggested letting libxml2 decide if a version string is valid, and the patch follows this.
Oracle accepts any version string and Db2 accepts only '1.0', so the patch sits between the two.
brief.thread_state: Tom Lane answered the first design question about validation. Since then the author has posted only rebases, and solai v tested v9 and found no problems, but nobody has reviewed the code or the design.
unclear: v1 skipped the version check in CONTENT mode while v10 checks in both modes, and the thread never discusses the change.
The patch prose does not show the ruleutils.c deparse output, such as how views using the new clauses dump and restore.
The doc says CONTENT mode may emit a declaration that the XML spec would not allow, and the patch prose does not say if this matches the standard.
The patch prose does not say how the options combine with INDENT, which reserializes the value.
The patch prose does not say if the new keywords are reserved or affect existing identifiers.

objections.title: Most of the result is reachable today with xmlroot() and string functions
objections.failure_scenario: A user who needs a declaration with a chosen version can already run `xmlserialize(document xmlroot(x, version '1.0', standalone no) as text)`, or prepend a literal `<?xml version="1.0"?>` with `||`. To drop a declaration, they can use `regexp_replace` on the serialized text. The patch adds keywords and a second way to set the version that core must keep consistent with `xmlroot`.
objections.argument: Postgres already has `xmlroot(xml, version ..., standalone ...)`, which sets the version in a value's XML declaration before serialization. The thread names no user who needs the new clauses (messages #1-#14), and the only stated motivation is marking X076 and X078 as supported. Standard conformance is a real reason, so this is not fatal, but a committer would likely ask what the clauses give beyond `xmlroot` plus string handling, and whether two version mechanisms validate the version string the same way.
objections.author_must_show: Which real use case cannot be met by xmlroot() plus xmlserialize() or simple string functions, and do both paths accept and reject the same version strings?

critic.reasoning: xmlroot() already sets or clears the version in a value's declaration before serialization, so the alternative can do most of the job. The thread does not compare the two paths or say if they validate version strings the same way.

objections.title: CONTENT mode can emit a declaration no XML parser accepts
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs xmlserialize(CONTENT '<a/><b/>text'::xml AS text INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION) to feed an external consumer. The output is '<?xml version="1.0"?><a/><b/>text'. That is not a well-formed document, and as an external entity its text declaration lacks the encoding that XML 1.0 requires, so the consumer's parser rejects it at load time.
objections.argument: The v10 doc states that in CONTENT mode the declaration is emitted "even if it would not normally be considered valid by the XML specification". The same patch flips X078 to YES in sql_features.txt, so information_schema.sql_features reports full support. The proposal does not say what SQL/XML requires for CONTENT with INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION, or why emitting malformed output is better than raising an error or documenting a deviation. Nobody discussed this in the thread after message #3.
objections.author_must_show: What does SQL/XML specify for CONTENT values that are not well-formed documents under INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION, and does the patch match it?

critic.reasoning: The v10 doc itself says CONTENT mode may emit a declaration the XML specification does not allow, while X078 becomes YES. Postgres already accepts such values, which lowers the severity, but nobody in the thread says what SQL/XML requires here.

objections.title: VERSION '1.1', a value the standard names, raises a WARNING
objections.failure_scenario: An application ported from another SQL/XML implementation uses VERSION '1.1' INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION in a bulk export. Every call returns a WARNING built from libxml2's parser message. If the warning fires per row, the client and server log fill with noise, and drivers that surface warnings report a problem for valid standard SQL.
objections.argument: Message #1 quotes the standard: the literal "shall be '1.0' or '1.1'". The patch delegates validity to libxml2, as Tom Lane suggested in message #2. As a result, a standard-sanctioned value is flagged as suspect, and the wording of the warning depends on the libxml2 build. The proposal does not say if the check runs once at parse time on the literal or for each evaluated row.
objections.author_must_show: Is the version checked once per statement or once per row, and why should a standard-listed value like '1.1' produce a warning at all?

critic.reasoning: Tom Lane's reply in message #2 covers who decides validity, but it does not cover a user-visible warning for '1.1', which the standard names. The per-row part belongs to maintenance-fit-2.

objections.title: Version check may run, and warn, once per row
objections.failure_scenario: A report runs xmlserialize(... VERSION '1.1' INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION) over a million-row table. If the check runs in the executor for each value, the query parses an extra document per row and sends a million WARNING messages to the client and server log.
objections.argument: The files touched include execExprInterp.c and xml.c, and the prose says libxml2 parses a minimal document to validate the version. The prose does not say if this happens once at parse or plan time or for every value. The SQL/XML clause takes a character string literal, so a single check before execution looks possible.
objections.author_must_show: Is the VERSION string validated once per statement or once per evaluated value, and how many warnings does a multi-row query emit?

critic.reasoning: The patch touches execExprInterp.c and the examples show the warning at run time. The prose does not say if the check runs once per statement or once per value.

objections.title: Replacing a declaration may drop the input's standalone attribute
objections.failure_scenario: A stored document starts with '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>'. An export job adds VERSION '1.0' INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION. If the rewritten declaration is version-only, standalone="yes" is lost, and a downstream validator now fetches the external DTD and applies its defaults. The user finds out only when downstream results change.
objections.argument: The commit message says the declaration is "added, replaced or removed" and that a written declaration never has an encoding. It does not say what happens to standalone. The encoding omission is justified by xml_out(), but that reason does not cover standalone, which carries document semantics and is not affected by encoding conversion.
objections.author_must_show: When VERSION or INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION replaces an existing declaration, is the input's standalone value kept, and is that what the standard requires?

critic.reasoning: The commit message and doc explain the missing encoding but do not mention standalone. The scenario depends on behavior the prose does not state, so it stands as a question the patch must answer.

refuted.title: Accepted VERSION strings depend on the installed libxml2 release
refuted.failure_scenario: A user creates a view using xmlserialize(... VERSION '1.1' INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION), which gives a warning on today's libxml2. A later distribution upgrade ships a libxml2 that treats '1.1' differently, so the query now errors or behaves silently differently. The user finds out at runtime after an OS update, with no Postgres change involved.
refuted.argument: The commit message says libxml2 parses a minimal document to decide between error and warning. So the meaning of a new SQL clause depends on a library the project does not control. Message #2 suggested deferring to libxml2, but it did not ask that libxml2's message text and its rules for an unsupported version become user-visible SQL behavior. The project already carries libxml2 version differences in alternative regression outputs, and this adds more surface to that cost.
refuted.author_must_show: Which libxml2 versions were tested, and does the error/warning split for '1.0', '1.1' and '2.0' stay the same across all of them?

critic.reasoning: In message #2 a committer proposed libxml2 as the authority on version strings, as Postgres already does for xml input. The scenario of a future libxml2 release changing how it treats '1.1' is speculation with no support in the material.

refuted.title: No user who needs these options is named in two years
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer adds VERSION and the new XMLDECLARATION keyword to the grammar, ruleutils.c deparse and xml.c. If almost nobody uses them, the code still needs fixes when libxml2 changes how it handles version strings. Users who need a declaration today already add or strip it with string functions on the text result.
refuted.argument: The only motivation in message #1 and the commit message is that X076 and X078 are listed as unsupported, and that Oracle and Db2 have them. Other databases having a feature counts as some demand, and standard conformance is an accepted reason in Postgres. But across 14 messages and 11 CommitFests, no user report, -general thread or production case asks for this. Message #12 confirms the patch works, not that anyone needs it.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or applications need a declaration with a chosen version, why does concatenating or stripping it on the text result not work for them, and how many are there?

critic.reasoning: The material shows evidence the rubric counts as demand: two SQL/XML standard features that Oracle and Db2 implement, per message #1. The remaining question, what the clauses add over existing functions, is covered by already-exists-1.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: sql_features.txt marks X076 and X078 as supported, and new XmlExpr fields change stored view rules.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes node definitions in primnodes.h and parsenodes.h, which extensions that inspect XmlExpr see.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch adds the SQL/XML clauses VERSION and INCLUDING/EXCLUDING XMLDECLARATION, with new keywords in kwlist.h.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: ruleutils.c must deparse the new clauses so that views using them dump and restore; the output is not shown.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The error or warning for a version string comes from libxml2, and xmlroot() already sets the version by another path.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch touches execExprInterp.c, and the libxml2 version check may run for each evaluated value.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: xmlroot() plus xmlserialize() already sets a declaration version, so part of the result exists today.

questions: What does SQL/XML require for INCLUDING XMLDECLARATION on a CONTENT value that is not a well-formed document, and does the patch match it?
What do the new clauses give that xmlroot() plus xmlserialize() does not, and do both paths accept and reject the same version strings?
Is the VERSION string checked once per statement or once per evaluated value, and how many warnings does a multi-row query emit?
Why does VERSION '1.1', a value the standard names, raise a warning, and why did v10 start checking the version in CONTENT mode?
When a declaration is replaced, is the input's standalone value kept, and how do the options combine with INDENT?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows xml.c, the libxml2 integration and the SQL/XML grammar would have to own it. Tom Lane answered one validation question in message #2 and has not reviewed the patch.
committability.liability: The owner signs for new keywords, the deparse of the new clauses in stored views, and user-visible errors and warnings that libxml2 produces, for as long as XMLSERIALIZE exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The author has rebased the patch through 11 CommitFests up to v10, which suggests he stays for fixes.

priority.reason: The patch adds two standard SQL/XML features for a small group of XML users, and its cost falls mostly on those users. It has waited through 11 CommitFests with a tester but no design review, so it needs a committer who knows the xml code.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review could not check if the new keywords are reserved, what ruleutils.c emits for views, or where the version check runs. Only 3 of 14 messages were shown, so later discussion may answer some questions.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Declarative partitioning
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Simon Riggs, Alvaro Herrera, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add declarative partitioning to PostgreSQL: a partitioned table kind with a LIST or RANGE partition key, created with CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY and CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF ... FOR VALUES, with partition key and bound information stored in new catalogs pg_partitioned_rel and pg_partition. Inserts and COPY route tuples to the right partition directly, while many ALTER TABLE operations, triggers, constraints and indexes on partitions are restricted; the WIP patch had no planner support yet.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for planner/optimization support, regression tests, and documentation or README files explaining the design before a full review. Simon Riggs held that the optimization side was the core of the design and recommended "Returned with Feedback" pending that work. Later messages asked for an incremental approach instead of one very large patch, and for a catalog structure and syntax that could later support multi-level partitioning. The CF manager then marked the patch returned with feedback, as the consensus was to rework it further.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The current patch implements a
bunch of stuff, but its hard to say what, how or why it does it and without
the planner stuff its all moot.

precedents_retrieved.title: Added support of XML_PARSE_HUGE flag for XML documents
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch passes the libxml2 XML_PARSE_HUGE flag when Postgres parses XML, which raises the single text node limit from 10,000,000 to 1,000,000,000. It replaces xmlParseBalancedChunkMemory(), which takes no options, with xmlNewNode() plus xmlParseInNodeContext() on a fake root node, and moves from xmlParseMemory() to xmlReadMemory().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The XML_PARSE_HUGE change was committed to HEAD as 2197d06224a1 and then reverted in f2743a7d70e7. The security team found that it lets the backend use large amounts of CPU and memory in cases like the billion laughs attack, even when the application checks input size, because libxml2 does not guarantee input limits under XML_PARSE_HUGE. The author agreed with the revert. The separate replacement of xmlSubstituteEntitiesDefault() with XML_PARSE_NOENT (65c5864d7fac) stayed in.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The security team has discussed 2197d06224a1 after a report from coverity regarding the effects that issues like [1] would create in the backend, and concluded that this patch should be reverted because this could cause the backend to waste plently of CPU and/or memory even if the application applied checks on the size of the data given in input, and libxml2 does not offer guarantees that input limits are respected under XML_PARSE_HUGE.

precedents_retrieved.title: Declarative partitioning
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds declarative range and list partitioning: a new partitioned relkind created with PARTITION BY, partitions created with CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF ... FOR VALUES, and new catalogs pg_partitioned_rel and pg_partition. It also covers multi-level partitioning, attach and detach of partitions, and tuple routing on insert through the parent.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas marked it Returned with Feedback near the 9.6 feature freeze. The last patch was posted on February 17, the entry had been Waiting on Author since March 2, and syntax, scope and performance testing were still open. He said he would review it for 9.7.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Even if we had a
new patch in hand at this point, I don't think there's any real chance
of being able to get this done for 9.6; there are too many things left
to do here in terms of figuring out syntax and scope, and of course
performance testing.

precedents_retrieved.title: ECPG: Declare Statement
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add DECLARE STATEMENT support to ECPG, so that an AT clause given once binds a statement name to a connection. Later PREPARE, EXECUTE, DECLARE CURSOR and similar statements then use that connection without repeating AT, with ecpglib functions such as ECPGdo changed to look up the connection by statement name.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They end in November 2016 with Michael Meskes waiting for a patch after the design was clarified, and the entry was returned with feedback in November 2017.

precedents_retrieved.title: SERIALIZABLE on standby servers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE transactions on standby servers by having the primary write snapshot safety information into commit records and separate WAL records. The standby waits for a point in the WAL stream where a snapshot is known to be safe, using hypothetical transactions that the primary tracks as stand-ins for standby transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author called the patch prototype/WIP code with unsolved problems. Two of them are a race between the safety decision and the order of commit records in WAL, and the absence of snapshot safety information in checkpoints. A third is that the primary makes transactions visible in ProcArrayEndTransaction() order while the standby uses commit record order, which can allow serialization anomalies. No review of the general approach came, and the entry was later withdrawn; the visible messages do not show who withdrew it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And that's precisely the issue: on the primary, transactions become visible to other transactions in the order in which they perform ProcArrayEndTransaction(), but on the standby, they become visible in the order in which they RecordTransactionCommit().

precedents_retrieved.title: Add code indentation check to cirrus-ci
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a Cirrus CI task, or a step in the SanityCheck or CompilerWarnings task, that runs pgindent and fails when a change is not pgindent-clean. The goal is to catch indentation problems in developer and cfbot CI runs before commit, so that committers spend less time on follow-up indentation fixes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CI check puts the burden of pgindent-cleanliness on initial patch submitters, while it should be enforced at commit into the master repo. He feared it would drive novice contributors away. Andrew Dunstan saw no consensus for the change, and the author withdrew the CF entry because the idea was being discussed in a separate thread about meson targets for pgindent.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We want to enforce this at commit into the master repo, but
I fear enforcing it earlier will drive novice contributors away for
no very good reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add llvm version into the version string
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the LLVM version to PG_VERSION_STR, the way the gcc version is already shown, so that JIT bug reports include it. A later version takes the runtime version from the loaded library through LLVMGetVersion, an API that exists from LLVM 16 on.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the configure-time llvm-config version may not match the library loaded at run time. He also objected that changing what version() returns can break code that parses it, and that adding subsystem versions to it does not scale to ICU or libxml2. He suggested a new system view instead, the author agreed to try that direction, and others proposed showing both build-time and runtime versions in the view.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Adding rows to a view over time seems way less likely to cause
problems than messing with a string people probably have crufty
parsing code for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Create shorthand for including all extra tests
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an 'all' value for PG_TEST_EXTRA, checked through a new check_extra_tests_enabled() function in Test/Utils.pm, so a full run includes every extra test suite. After feedback it replaced 'all' with a 'needs-private-lo' category that enables the kerberos, ldap, load_balance and ssl tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the extra tests are excluded by default because they are security hazards, so each should be reviewed before it is enabled. Peter Eisentraut said 'needs-private-lo' is not the only condition, since kerberos and ldap need extra software and load_balance may need edits to the hosts file. He also preferred each test deciding on its own over a central mapping, and saw no sensible grouping for six values. The author agreed to revisit the idea if more PG_TEST_EXTRA options appear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So someone would still need to familiarize themselves with these tests
individually before setting a global option like this.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at XMLSERIALIZE VERSION or XML declaration options. The thread cites no earlier discussion of this idea, so this angle gives no objection.
Keyword reservation and ruleutils.c deparse (pg_dump of views) could not be judged from the prose. Both are listed as unclear, and no failure can be shown without the code.

The patch adds no persistent or cross-node state: no WAL, no on-disk format change, no wire protocol change and no catalog columns. Its only stored effect is new XmlExpr fields in stored view rules, which need the usual catversion bump; ruleutils.c deparse covers pg_dump, though its output is not shown.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect: the new options only change the text of the caller's own XMLSERIALIZE result, with no new data access, catalog state, or code run by other roles. Libxml2 checks the version string, so the brief gives no input that could escape the declaration.

The feature is small, standard-defined (X076, X078) and limited to XMLSERIALIZE, so non-users pay almost nothing. No committer has reviewed the design since message #2, which affects committability but is not an objection to the idea.
One objection. The new clauses are SQL-standard XMLSERIALIZE syntax, and no extension can add grammar, so core placement is justified if the features are wanted.
Demand is thin but standards conformance and Oracle/Db2 parity give some motivation. Costs fall mostly on feature users, so this is a 'not now, show demand' point, not a rejection.
